newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady, holding one-year lows.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady, holding one-year lows.

text.p: Brent crude futures were untraded in Asia around midday on Wednesday, as players moved to the sidelines after London prices dropped to one-year lows.
July Brent on SIMEX was quoted at $17.42/$17.58 per barrel.
London slumped to $17.45 overnight -- the lowest level since May 20, 1996 -- before recovering slightly to settle at $17.50, for a loss on the day of six cents.
Brokers said the market was showing signs of consolidating, despite Brent's fall overnight, which was likely to mean downside potential was now limited.
NYMEX dropped just one cent in New York to $18.67 and had recovered three cents on ACCESS to $18.70, indicating selling pressure was abating.

API data showed a bigger than expected build in gasoline, which could start to weigh on the market in coming weeks. The build halved a year-on-year deficit and is gradually erasing support for the gasoline price.
Gasoline was last traded on ACCESS at 56.10 cents per gallon, down 0.30 from New York and erasing the overnight 0.20 gain.
